problem:
Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations

$$
x={u}^{2},\,y=2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,z=u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\ge 0,\,0\le v<2\pi ,
$$

at the point $(1,0,1).$
worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩,\,u\ge 0,\,0\le v<2\pi .
$$

First, notice that since $(1,0,1)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}=1 \\ 2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v=0 \\ u\operatorname{cos}⁡v=1\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=0.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-u\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,0) & =⟨2(1),\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡0,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡0⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,0) & =⟨0,\,2(1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(0),\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,0)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,0) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,0,\,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-2,\,0,\,4⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ (-2)\cdot (x-1)+0\cdot y+4\cdot (z-1) & =0 \\ -2x+4z-2 & =0 \\ -x+2z-1 & =0 \\ x-2z & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
